label: t2-patterns-law
topic: Track 2 (E. coli chemotactic range-expansion front) mapped against law set 1.8.1, with a new checked Lean law
summary: Law set 1.8.1 (59 pinned laws: 36 accepted, 10 candidate, 7 proposed, 3 retired, 3 contested; 14 have no theorem) contains NO accepted law about spatial patterns or fronts. Directly relevant are two pinned candidates, fisher-kpp-speed (Delphi.LeanBio.Round2.KppSpeed.kpp_min_speed) and turing-ddi (Delphi.LeanBio.Round2.TuringDDI.turing_instability). turing-wavelength has a registry file but is NOT pinned in 1.8.1. The older map (laws-patterns.json, read at 1.6.0 from the split-out leanbio copy) cites Delphi/Turing.lean and Delphi/CellGeometry.lean, which do not exist in the application repo; it listed Fisher-KPP speed as missing, but it is now pinned as a candidate. The older map missed the Narla closed form and every law a chemotactic front actually needs. I wrote and checked NarlaSpeed.lean (namespace Delphi.Track2.ChemotaxisFront): from the Narla closed form c^2 (X+Da) = X^2 r A it proves that front speed goes as the square root of growth rate (ratio law, strict monotonicity, quadrupling doubles speed, log-log slope exactly 1/2) and an elimination lemma (a 1.5-fold faster front cannot come from at most 2-fold faster growth at fixed X, Da, A). Checker: errors=0, sorryAx=0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for all 10 theorems; a sorry-mutated copy was correctly rejected.
lay_summary: We have a library of mathematical rules that a computer has checked line by line. Almost none of them talk about colonies of bacteria spreading across a plate, so the library was nearly blind to this track. The nearest rule says how fast a wave of growth plus random wandering can spread, and it gives only a slow baseline: the real chemotactic front is about five times faster. I added one new checked rule. It says that if bacteria steer toward food, the front speed should grow like the square root of how fast they multiply, so doubling the growth rate should speed the front by only about 41 percent. Earlier lab numbers on this project suggest the real exponent is closer to one, which means the simple rule may fail, and that is exactly what a good test should be able to show.

glossary.plain: A proof-checking program: a statement counts only if the computer verifies every step.
The hidden placeholder Lean uses when a proof has a gap; its presence means the proof is not finished.
A frozen, numbered list of the rules the project trusts at a given moment.
Registry stages: candidate is machine-checked but not human-approved; accepted is approved; proposed is only an idea with no proof.
A registry entry that names a topic but has no proved theorem behind it.
The moving edge where a colony spreads into fresh territory.
Cells steering up a gradient of a food chemical.
A front driven by growth plus random spreading, moving at a fixed speed.
Spots or stripes that appear when two chemicals spread at different rates.
How many percent one quantity changes when another changes by one percent.
A theorem that says a stated combination of numbers is impossible, so a design that commits to it can be rejected.

findings.claim: Law set 1.8.1 pins 59 laws: 36 accepted, 10 candidate, 7 proposed, 3 retired, 3 contested.

Exactly 14 pinned laws have no Lean theorem: aspect-ratio-induced-drag, disc-flying-fish-fin-ratio-gap, disc-heterurus-mass-exponent, disc-measured-wing-loading-band, disc-pectoral-length-allometry, elastic-similarity, fick-principle (module set, theorem null), fin-length-ratio, gene-regulatory-dynamics, gill-o2-uptake, muscle-power-premise, taxiing-thrust, test-loop-only-density-sanity, walking-pendulum-speed. None bears on spatial patterns except gene-regulatory-dynamics, a 'gap' entry for how a gene edit changes a structure.
findings.evidence_quote: How a gene edit changes a structure quantitatively (bioelectric kcnk5b, slc43a2a transport).

findings.claim: fisher-kpp-speed v1.1.0, status candidate, pinned since 1.8.0, no approval; theorem Delphi.LeanBio.Round2.KppSpeed.kpp_min_speed in lean/registry/proposals/fisher-kpp-speed/law.lean; hypothesis c^2 = 4 s D; constraint KPP1 (c^2 >= 4 s D). Bears on the growth-plus-diffusion baseline of the front (Narla's model reduces to a Fisher wave without chemotaxis). Axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] per its result.json.
findings.evidence_quote: For a Fisher-KPP gene wave with dispersal coefficient D > 0, selection coefficient s > 0 and minimal speed c > 0 satisfying c^2 = 4*s*D (a named hypothesis)

findings.claim: The KPP baseline for this track is far below the measured chemotactic front: with D_rho = 0.1807 mm^2/h, r = 0.9985 /h, 2 sqrt(r D) = 0.8495 mm/h versus measured 4.335 mm/h, a factor 5.1. So KPP1 would not be violated but is nowhere near binding. Inputs are taken from design-patterns.json (not re-fetched by me).
findings.source: own calculation scripts/t2-patterns-law/kpp_vs_narla.py using numbers in D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents/design-patterns.json

findings.claim: turing-ddi v1.1.0, candidate, pinned since 1.8.0; theorem Delphi.LeanBio.Round2.TuringDDI.turing_instability (conclusion: exists q>0 with disp<0, and du != dv), module lean/registry/proposals/turing-ddi/law.lean; constraint TURING1. Bears on this track only if a two-morphogen synthetic circuit is added; the Narla/Cremer front is a chemotaxis-growth travelling wave, not a Turing system.
findings.value: TURING1: Dv f_u + Du g_v > 2 sqrt(Du Dv det J)
findings.evidence_quote: there is a strictly positive squared wavenumber at which the dispersion relation is negative, so the homogeneous state is linearly unstable to a spatial mode

findings.claim: turing-wavelength v1.1.0 (candidate, theorem Delphi.LeanBio.Round2.TuringWavelength.onset_wavenumber, constraint TURINGLAMBDA1) has a registry file with introduced_in null and is NOT among the 59 pins of lawset-1.8.1.json, so it is not in the current law set.

findings.claim: The older map cites lean/Delphi/Turing.lean (turing_instability_iff, no_instability_of_equal_diffusivity, trace_neg_of_wellMixed, exists_pos_growth_of_D_neg), lean/Delphi/CellGeometry.lean (tripleJunction_120, hexagon_of_120, etc.) and registry ids turing-ddi-linear-condition and seven cell-geometry ids. None of these files or ids exist in the application repo at 1.8.1: lean/Delphi has no Turing.lean or CellGeometry.lean (only Altitude, Audit, Blueprint, Certificates, Constraints, Empirical, Favored, Fisher, Flight, Genotype, Hydrostatics, Kimura, MaynardSmith, Perturb, Physiology, Scaling, Thompson), there is no ThompsonLaws or DarwinLaws library, and the registry has turing-ddi (a different, weaker theorem: one direction, hypothesis-form) instead. Those files do exist in the older split-out copy upstream/leanbio/lean/Delphi/ (Turing.lean, CellGeometry.lean, Crystals.lean listed). So the older map's strongest law (the iff characterisation) is not available to this application's checker.

The older map listed 'Fisher-KPP front speed' as a missing law. It now exists in 1.8.1 as the pinned candidate fisher-kpp-speed (introduced 1.8.0), but only as the algebraic minimum of the linear speed relation under hypothesis c^2 = 4sD; it does not prove travelling-wave existence and has nothing on chemotaxis.
findings.evidence_quote: it does not establish that a travelling wave exists, that compactly supported initial data converge to it, or that any population disperses diffusively.

findings.claim: Other pinned laws touching the track only marginally: maynardsmith-hitchhiking (candidate, Delphi.LeanBio.Hitchhiking.hitchhiking_relHet, lean/registry/proposals/maynardsmith-hitchhiking/law.lean) and kimura-fixation-probability (accepted, Delphi.NeutralChain.fixedBy_tendsto, lean/Delphi/Kimura.lean) and favored-fixation-lower-bound (accepted, Delphi.FavoredChain.fixationProbability_ge, lean/Delphi/Favored.lean) for edge sectoring/genetic drift at the front (the scout's runner-up); physiology-q10 (accepted, Delphi.Physiology.q10_ratio, lean/Delphi/Physiology.lean) for temperature scaling of growth and motility; development-growth-asymptote (candidate, von Bertalanffy, Exocoetidae-scoped, binds nothing) is NOT a fit for logistic colony growth.

What the older map missed (relative to 1.8.1 and to the chosen system): (1) it mapped the wrong library version, so it names files and ids absent from 1.8.1; (2) it never mentions turing-ddi, turing-wavelength or fisher-kpp-speed by their real registry ids; (3) it has no law for the Narla/Keller-Segel closed form that the design's frozen predictions F1 to F3 actually use; (4) it contains no check of the square-root-of-growth-rate law, which is the control law the design says the data already contradict.
findings.source: laws-patterns.json keys (existing, missing, elimination_pattern, changes_since_october) read in this run

findings.claim: Narla et al. state a square-root dependence of the expansion speed on growth rate and on the relative attractant concentration, and that speed does not depend on the uptake rate.
findings.source: Europe PMC full text PMC8640786, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC8640786/fullTextXML (fetched in this run, 315460 bytes, sha256 17ca8bac191814334ace7abe484087836bbfdb141c5b960d6628b22965424054, saved scratch/t2-patterns-law/narla.xml)
findings.evidence_quote: there is a square root dependence on the growth rate r, as validated by numerical results in Fig. 2A.

findings.claim: I did NOT independently re-derive or re-read Narla Eq. 21 from the MathML; the closed form c = X sqrt(r A/(X+Da)) is taken from the design file's transcription, with only the sqrt-in-r dependence confirmed from the paper text. The Lean law is therefore a theorem about the stated form, labelled as a named hypothesis.

Using the design's fitted X = 0.7874 mm^2/h, Da = 2.88 mm^2/h, A = 100, r = 0.9985 /h, Eq 21 gives c = 4.109 mm/h and c^2/r = 16.906 mm^2/h, matching the design's fitted k = 16.907 (the fit was to this relation) and 5.2 percent below the measured 4.335 mm/h.
